options.misconception: names "A shared road" where the rule requires "A factory emitting smoke affecting neighbors"

options.text: A factory emitting smoke affecting neighbors

questions.explanation: Factory smoke is a negative production externality. Vaccines are positive, roads are common resources.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Cartographer's projection 56 asks which is a positive consumption externality. Which?

options.text: A private good with no spillovers
options.misconception: selects "A private good with no spillovers" instead of "A student getting vaccinated and protecting others"

options.text: A student getting vaccinated and protecting others

options.misconception: names "A congested bridge" where the rule requires "A student getting vaccinated and protecting others"

questions.explanation: Vaccination protects others, a positive consumption externality. Pollution is negative; congestion is common.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A study guide on reading a benefit-cost ratio supplies the following figures for analysis. ratio 1.25 and cost 200. Net benefit?
questions.explanation: The rule that settles this reading a benefit-cost ratio item is: Compute benefit then subtract cost. That is why "50" is the answer.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Cartographer's projection 58 asks why information is often asymmetric in markets. Explain.

answer.exemplar: Sellers often know more about product quality than buyers, and buyers cannot easily verify claims before purchase, creating information asymmetry.

questions.explanation: Applying the asymmetric information rule — Sellers know more; verification is costly — yields "Sellers often know more about product quality than buyers, and buyers cannot easily verify claims before purchase, creating information asymmetry". Reversing the reasoning would recover the given quantities.
questions.hint: Sellers know more; verification is costly.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Cartographer's projection 59 asks how to reduce the lemons problem. Which helps?

options.misconception: selects "Hiding quality information" instead of "Mandatory disclosure or certification"
selects "Banning all sales" instead of "Mandatory disclosure or certification"

questions.explanation: The adverse selection and lemons principle here is: Reveal quality to fix lemons. On that basis "Mandatory disclosure or certification" is correct, while "Hiding quality information" selects "Hiding quality information" instead of "Mandatory disclosure or certification".

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Cartographer's projection 60 asks how coinsurance reduces moral hazard. Explain.

answer.exemplar: Coinsurance makes the insured pay a share of costs, so they retain an incentive to avoid risky behavior, reducing moral hazard.

questions.explanation: The rule that settles this moral hazard item is: Shared cost preserves care incentives. That is why "Coinsurance makes the insured pay a share of costs, so they retain an incentive to avoid risky behavior, reducing moral hazard" is the answer.
